candidate.answerReason: Single women, wives, and married men have relative counts 2:3:3, so married men form 3/8 of all people.

methods.label: Use equal shares of the population
methods.explanation:
A randomly selected woman is single with probability \(\frac25\), so \(\frac25\) of the women are single and the remaining \(\frac35\) are wives. Thus single women and wives are in the ratio \(2:3\).

Every wife at the party has her husband there, so the numbers of wives and married men are equal. Consequently, single women, wives, and married men are in the ratio
\[
2:3:3.
\]
These three groups include everyone at the party. They total \(2+3+3=8\) equal shares, of which married men occupy \(3\). Therefore the required fraction is \(\frac38\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: The given probability is interpreted as a fraction of women, then elementary ratios account for the husbands.

candidate.annotationRationale: The main target is comparing group counts while changing the reference whole from women to all people. Equally likely probability supplies the initial fraction of women, and fraction meaning supports the final part-over-total interpretation.

review.mathematicalCheck: The women consist of single women and wives in ratio 2:3. Each wife has one husband present, so single women, wives, and married men have ratio 2:3:3. These exhaust the room, giving married men fraction 3/8, choice B.
